To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of national accounts for estimating household spending on health care is possible, but requires careful consideration and adjustment.

(1) the use of NA for estimating household spending on health requires a thorough understanding of differences in concepts used in NA and CA/HA; (2) NA can be used for verifying the plausibility of the household spending estimates of CA/HA; and (3) the use of the NA for estimating household health spending requires the use of a consistent methodology and the use of the same sources as in the CA/HA, and the availability of a comprehensive and reliable supply side.
NA and HA are complementary, that the use of NA in HA is not a panacea, but that it is a good starting point for the development of health accounts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparability of data on health expenditure from national and health accounts.
the question whether NA can be used as an alternative for HA.
the question of whether NA or CA&HA data should be used for policy purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NA can be used for the estimation of health spending, but that this depends on the quality of the data and the context of the policy measures.
NA and HA are not compatible, and that NA data should be used with caution for HA purposes.
both frameworks have a role to play.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the comparability of data between NA and HA can be improved by using a consistent approach for the estimation of consumption of human health.
NA are a useful tool for validating HA and for estimating household spending in countries where the latter is not available.
, although the two frameworks are different, they have a lot to offer each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
comparability of data is not only a technical issue but is strongly related to policy.
it is not possible to use NA and HA without adjustments.
comparability of data can be achieved if the specificities of the two frameworks are understood and taken into account.
